title: Forspoken
description: Forspoken is an action RPG that follows the journey of Frey, a young New Yorker transported to the beautiful and cruel land of Athia.  In search of a way home, Frey must use her newfound magical abilities to traverse sprawling landscapes, battle monstrous creatures and defeat powerful matriarchs known as Tantas.

critic_reviews.quote: Forspoken is absolutely fantastic. With all the spells you can unlock, the gear you can upgrade, the fights, the bosses, and a storyline that rivals the best video game stories, this isn't a return to form for SquareEnix, it's a testament that they still got it, and will have it for a very, very long time.

Forspoken is an incredible title. Although the story suffers from being a bit too generic, the gameplay is inventive, magical, and an absolute blast. This is a game I’ll come back to again and again just to move around and exist in the fascinating fantasy world. Forspoken is an exciting leap forward for action games, and I can’t get enough of it.
Forspoken manages to stand out for its fantastic combat system and spectacular exploration in its open world. However, it clearly could have been better in other areas.
Forspoken feels like a breath of fresh air for open-world adventures with its stylish engine, but is held back by pacing and other foibles.

There's a lot to love about Forspoken despite its technical issues. It makes up for that with great traversal, a fantastic DualSense implementation, and solid storytelling. It might not be for everyone, but I enjoyed my time in Athia and will be checking out the story DLC when it launches in the future.

It’s always going to be on my desktop or my PlayStation, and I’m gonna keep going back to it every once in a while because it’s really relaxing to hold down the parkour button and go through this huge world to unlock stuff and find new quests.

Forspoken is an urban-come-high-fantasy open-world, action-adventure game played in the third person. Combining magic and parkour, you take on the role of Frey as she learns to understand her new abilities in a strange world that needs saving from disaster.
Forspoken presents a genuinely human story blended well with combat and a variety of exploration options, setting it up to be PlayStation’s next big franchise.

Forspoken doesn’t do anything new for the open-world genre of games, but it does offer just enough to distinguish itself, mostly thanks to Frey and her magic spells, and a story that’s able to stick the landing. Or to translate this to Whedonspeak, “Yep, she really did just do that!"

Forspoken is a unique game, with a very distinct gameplay, setting and story that compose a very fun and interesting experience. It suffers with its short duration, problemactic camera, lack of variety in side missions and it needs a few adjustments to its gameplay, but its one of the most beautiful games on the PS5 so far and a title that deserves everyone's attention.

You can spend hours completing spell challenges, exploring dungeons, fighting enemies, and activating altars to upgrade your powers. But that fun is often held back by the story. Forspoken's pacing could be better. The game takes you away from what you want to do. We often wanted to explore to our heart's content, but the game forced us to spend minutes that felt like forever in uninteresting storytelling.
Want to explore a beautiful and desolate fantasy world without being stomped into the ground by every enemy you meet? The power fantasy of 'Forspoken' might just be the game for you.

After all is said and done, Forspoken emerges as a solid new IP. It has its fair share of issues, but the longer you spend time in Athia, the more its world draws you in with its intriguing combat and the simple pleasure of freely crossing massive environments with spellbinding abilities. Luminous Productions is definitely onto something with this concept, it just needs a bit more focus and refinement. At the very least, Forspoken proves its worth on its own terms, and demonstrates the potential to someday hang alongside Square Enix’s staple franchises.

There was a moment in which we really feared for the success of Fospoken, which, due to a not exactly crystal clear communication from the publisher, often ended up making us feel mixed sensations. Confirming the impressions gained on the occasion of previous direct contacts with the product, however, the new creature of Luminous Productions convinces in every respect, without excelling in any field. While the staid pace of the isekai matrix plot is counterbalanced by surprising twists and turns that leave a love flavor, the albeit chaotic combat system and the exorbitant number of optional activities offered by an open world that is anything but empty compensate for a surrender visual not quite state of the art.

Forspoken represented a huge risk taken by newcomer Luminous Productions. While the story may feel a bit contrived at times, the Flow method of traversal and combat more than makes up for it. Frey may annoy some people as the protagonist, but stringing together a chain of magical commands within just a few seconds while deftly avoiding incoming fireballs is rewarding, and ultimately, I came away from Forspoken having enjoyed my time helping the people of Athia.

Forspoken is a game of ups and downs. The title is much more focused on the story than on the open world component and this is not a bad thing at all. The narrative is enjoyable, but not without flaws, while the open world is very classic in style without particular flashes of originality.

Forspoken it's not the next gen game that we're waiting for, but it's not as bad as some found in the demo. It has its share of elements to improve, starting with the script, but it makes combat and traverse very fresh and enjoyable, in a world full of things to do, that invites to keep playing even after watching the ending credits.

Forspoken is a far better and more compelling game than I had feared, but it also doesn’t reach the heights I dreamt of. There is a lot of fun to be had exploring Athia and the main quest keeps things interesting even when you get bored with the open-world checklist. But at the same time I can’t help but be disappointed with how safe Forspoken plays the open world, and I am unlikely to go back to clear out all of those rote points of interest. And I also can’t deny there are some eyebrow-raising moments as to how the writers chose to portray a black woman like Frey, despite personally liking her quite a bit when viewed through the lens of having finished the game. There is a lot of diversity in the cast too, in a way we don’t usually get from big-budget RPGs. I am not sure how many steps forward versus how many steps back Forspoken takes, but there are steps taken forward. In the end, I recommend Forspoken to anyone who loves Final Fantasy XV or Ubisoft-style open worlds and especially anyone who has a thing for character mobility. Yet, the game has a certain charm that I believe makes it worth giving a try to anyone.

Forspoken is therefore an experience that takes time to reveal its potential, but which, once the controls have been mastered, offers to discover a pleasant open world thanks to the magical powers of Frey.

Forspoken is an ambitious title that builds both its fluid movement and its battle system around the concept of magic. From comfortable exploration to speedy combat, this unique open world action RPG has plenty of appeal, and its story that depicts the spiritual growth of its young New Yorker protagonist is immersive. That being said, the game does have issues, such as a lack of variety in side quests and a hub area that takes too much time to navigate through.

Even with its unfortunate first impression, I’d (heartily) recommend Forspoken. Its exceptional gameplay is more than enough to make it worth playing and is all the more noteworthy, given it’s a fresh new IP. If nothing else, it lays the groundwork for a new series that has plenty to build from and could go on to be remembered for far more than some rough dialogue.
Rough and ready, just like Frey, Forspoken is a tale worth stomping through one high-stakes, magic-infused battle at a time.

Forspoken isn't for everyone - and this is its strength. Games that spark controversy can be the most interesting. This seems a sign that the developers have successfully realized their vision. Such courage is commendable, especially in the era of clones.

Early on, Forspoken‘s somewhat empty, barren world isn’t the most appealing. Stick with it, though, and you’ll be rewarded with more interesting landscapes, plenty of side content to sink your teeth into and a range of magical beasts itching for a fight. Frey makes a great protagonist, and we couldn’t help but be charmed by her punchy personality. But it’s her exhilarating parkour that really sets Forspoken apart. This open world adventure offers up the type of fun that’s hard to put down once you get started. We’re certainly keen to keep returning to Athia to mop up those remaining distractions.

As a new title from Luminous Productions six years after FFXV, Forspoken continues to show the shortcomings of its open-world design. The abundance of magical combat and the still-excellent story make up for most of these shortcomings. However, the hopes for a fantastic magical world cannot be fulfilled.
There's something here to get stuck into for fans of open world adventures, and Forspoken isn't without its charms, but like Frey herself, it's often its own worst enemy.
Forspoken is neither black nor white, it's a mottled gray of spectacular combat and magical parkour to be experienced within a dated open world.

Forspoken offers a unique and thrilling experience with its impressive combat and smooth traversal mechanics. The story and open world may fall victim to the pitfalls of its genre and the largely formulaic side quest design only shines occasionally, but it's an overall satisfying and well-crafted action RPG with fast-paced and energetic gameplay.

Forspoken's story and combat fail to reach the heights of its movement and exploration, but thankfully those two latter elements make up most of the experience. I sprinted, often literally, through the campaign in about 15 hours, and now I have a large world filled with nooks and crannies I'm eager to run through and explore. The narrative won’t linger with me, and I avoided combat in the open world often, but I loved making Frey leap and fly through Athia to discover all its treasure chests and secrets.

Forskpoken isn't a bad game, but it isn't outstanding either. If you get
interested in its universe, whether for its story or combat, it won't
leave you indifferent. However, the game doesn't dazzle, and it might
not meet the expectations of all players.

Forspoken is on the precipice of something great. Behind the funneled narrative beats and the obese, sprawling world is a game that simply wants players to engage with its every part. Past the eye-rolling dialog and self-serious narrative is a potentially interesting protagonist and universe that occasionally mesh well. Each puzzle piece of Forspoken is so close to fitting and so often I could see the picture clearly, especially when bounding across the seemingly boundless landscape, making the screen quiver and explode with Frey’s awe-inspiring magic. Perhaps in another place, in another time, Forspoken will speak to everyone.

My time with Forspoken was a strange one. Elements of the game are fantastic, with an engrossing story and a gorgeous world. However, it all just feels segmented, like nothing really wants to work together. Forspoken is a good game and one I would recommend to most open-world fans, but it just feels so close to greatness that I can’t help but walk away disappointed.

Forspoken is average. It has the highs and lows of an overall regular
gaming experience. The nods to Alice in Wonderland, the combat and Frey
Holland's story are pretty good, but the game fails to deliver next-gen
visuals and a better storytelling experience. There are so many fades to
black and cutscenes that you feel bored, especially during the first
hours of gameplay.
Nice fleshed combat and parkour, fun and very fast-paced fights. However, the open world and the activities within it are not as satisfying.

While the cheerful combat with cool parkour moves were exceptionally fun, Forspoken has been lacking in so many ways for players who have endured its delay announcement for twice. All those cute cats fill Frey's room only serve to double the loneliness that is already been full in Athian world.

The parkour and combat systems are worth developing further. Unfortunately, the developers fail to embed this groundbreaking approach into a convincing overall concept. Great moments are repeatedly thwarted by a lack of polish, a dull game world and an incredibly sluggish story.

Forspoken isn't without its hiccups—hit-or-miss side quests...and repetitive activities. Nevertheless, I enjoyed my time with Forspoken's focal storyline. The graphics, voice acting, and musical score are phenomenal, and the cat content is a lovely addition.

Forspoken feels like a test that was turned in with answers missing, returned with a big red "Finish Your Work" inked at the top. So much of the game feels like unrealized potential, a big, messy first draft. There are too many mechanics, there's too much story, too much empty world, and too little chance for surprise or discovery. However, I can't say I didn't enjoy a lot of my time with Forspoken. When the combat clicks, it can be a lot of fun. Forspoken is ambitious, and there are hints of a winning formula. I hope the developers keep chipping away at what doesn't work. It would be a shame if Forspoken is forsaken.

I would recommend Forspoken to action and RPG fans, but I wish I could give them one of my save files with total open-world freedom and most of the traversal and combat spells unlocked from the jump. The adventure is at its weakest when it's forcing players to wade through lots of poor narrative content that takes too long to pay off. Its best beats aren’t paced or delivered well and serve as a weighty vambrace holding back this game’s true magic: a dazzling open-world game that truly does feel next-gen.

Forspoken is vibrant, experimental, and undercooked all at once. It feels like a throwback to the Xbox 360-era of Square Enix games that were weird and experimental, like The Last Remnant and Infinite Undiscovery, only with a much bigger budget and flashier visuals. Its traversal and combat mechanics shine, but they’re trapped underneath a story and setting that feels painfully average and completely unwilling to engage with more challenging themes.
Despite its flaws, Forspoken is a fun adventure that nails the minute-to-minute gameplay with Frey’s parkour abilities and magic spells.

Forspoken is a fun action game that shines best when you're taking advantage of the great magic parkour to soar through the fantasy world of Athia and blast enemies with overwhelmingly cool spells. However, its content is underwhelming, its RPG systems are weak, and its visuals are less advanced than advertised. As such, Forspoken's potential is largely unrealized in its current state. It's still a decent romp for genre fans to go through, though waiting until it gets a discount or is added to one of the many subscription services is recommended.

Rather than letting its awful story simply be a good excuse for its excellent gameplay, Forspoken insists on constantly interrupting your fun to throw some truly bad exposition your way. Forspoken's character building and lore are a disaster but it manages to make it up with its incredible combat and traversal mechanics.

As a new IP, Forspoken comes off quite well. For example, the story and lore is very interesting, with the interactions between Frey and her bracelet Cuff being enjoyable. Add in magical combat and parkour, and it creates a game that can bring you a lot of fun. At the same time, you have to take into account a very weak beginning and that it is very recognizable in terms of gameplay design. That is, it's more of the same and in terms of variety not really extensive. As a result, Forspoken is a game that is worth playing, but at the same time it doesn't really excel or innovate in anything very much.

Truly a waste of potential. Forspoken gets saved by its spectacular combat and traversal mechanics, but the value of those systems gets skewered by a disappointing story and a trite open world structure. It's still a fun experience if you love experimenting with combat and magic, but we sincerely hope to see those systems recycled for something less rushed in the future.

Given the opportunity to dare, Forspoken chooses to play it incredibly safe, with muddled pacing and strict adherence to both narrative and gameplay tropes holding it back from reaching its groundbreaking potential. Regardless, its dazzling visuals, charismatic leads, memorable boss battles, and energetic and varied combat will reward the more patient player with a solid, spellbinding adventure… And, for everybody else, there are magical cats.

Luminous Productions clearly had a vision for Forspoken, and it shines through brilliantly when the player is unshackled and left to their own devices in the gorgeous game world, buoyed by Forspoken's atmospheric music. Unfortunately, the narrative's pacing has left it feeling as though it was significantly scaled back during development. Forspoken is sprawling, awing in its scale, and a treat to look at, and while the gameplay is snappy and engaging, it's not necessarily impressive enough to completely distract from haphazard discussions with NPCs and a narrative that should have been given more space.

Despite its flaws, I enjoyed my time with Forspoken. While the narrative is janky at times, the premise is compelling and the world of Athia is exceedingly well-built. The movement is where the game shines, making exploration a joy instead of a chore. The postgame is also surprisingly competent when it comes to dealing with the implications of the main story’s twists and turns, a rarity for open-world games. I didn’t know what to expect when I started playing Forspoken but I came out feeling satisfied.
Forspoken has a good foundation, with great combat design and parkour, but the contents of this world are not as good and, consequently, struggle to keep the player engaged.
The technology, which is impressive in places, stumbles over questionable design decisions, an uninspired game world and a combat system that is only visually exciting.
An adventure in which the need to conquer the lady and the altruistic obsession to save the world give way to more human interests, more visceral and easier to connect with.
Forspoken is a game that has great potential, expressed in a precise, fast and fun combat system. Sadly, everything else in the game lacks novelty or interest in exploration.

As Luminous Productions’ first project after being formed from the developers of Final Fantasy XV, Forspoken is a remarkable yet flawed experience. There’s so much potential here, with an outstanding magic parkour system and a beautiful open world. However, it’s clear that the ambition was a little too high for this studio, as there are just too many incomplete (but great) ideas at work here that just don’t come to fruition.
Forspoken is fun to play most of the time, but it's a damn shame that the game's remaining elements eagerly attempt to ruin that enjoyment at every turn.

Forspoken is a fun action RPG when it gets out of its own way. Its linear narrative and heavy-handed first few hours sap the player’s goodwill, before letting you free and realising its true potential. Strong combat and traversal mechanics really shine, and by the end, even the story manages to rise, like Frey herself, to the challenge.

Forspoken lacks the kind of refinement expected of a AAA title. If the concepts had received more attention, then the entire package would have been more cohesive. Still, despite its issues, there's definitely something here to enjoy if you can focus in on what the game does well: narrative, accessibility, and writing.
While Forspoken has its fair share of glaring issues, I have to admit that I still enjoyed my time with its warts and all, as it managed to entertain and engage me with its combat system alone.

Magical world with exciting and thrilling story that eventually delivers. But until it does deliver it feels forever. A must play for those who love action paced fluid combat and enjoy different vibrant colours but can overlook and tolerate few cheap scripts and few silly bugs.
With better pacing, slightly lighter tone and some self-restraint Forspoken would have been a much better game.

While Forspoken is a much better time than chatter on social media might suggest, those who opt to take on Frey’s journey will likely encounter bumps and stumbles that are hard to ignore, as well as have to deal with some unpleasant traveling companions strapped to their arms. Folks who can put up with those shortcomings, though, will find a dramatic and very pretty adventure as a stranger running freely across a strange land.

user_reviews.author: Rikkuo
user_reviews.quote: This game was a blast to play! Too bad the media outlets covered it poorly! Gorgeous open world, epic bosses and mobs, endless traversal, I would have play and boughten the sequel no questions asked!!

user_reviews.author: Ascarys
user_reviews.quote: There are a lot of naysayers on this game, but it's fantastically fun. The combat system is the best that Square has put out in a long while. Overall it's a fantastic RPG, putting FFXVI to absolute shame.

user_reviews.author: Lolinreallife
user_reviews.quote:
If I'm being honest, this game is a mid-to-hard 7, but I'll clock in as a soft 8 just to combat the onslaught of unfairly harsh criticism. By no means is this game groundbreaking, but it feels false to not acknowledge that its overwhelming negative reception was, at least, somewhat influenced by the political discourse at the time.

All that aside, Forspoken is an engaging and ambitious RPG, mixing open-world exploration with magical action-RPG combat and some parkour elements sprinkled into both. I played the game not long after its release in 2023, buying it on sell. I didn't expect much but I was still surprised as how enjoyable it was after the drawn-out introduction. I revisited the game recently to see if it was really as good as I remembered or if my positive memory was a contrarian fluke. 

While the story and environment feel familiar, I do really enjoy the world-building and magic system. There's no shortage of magic for the protagonist to use, and every magic element has multiple basic attacks and special attacks to use. Unfortunately, there's very little there in the parkour traversal system of the game. There's very little real parkour and more magically-enhanced free running and jumping/climing up steep obstacles. Though, I wish the controls for the magic system felt more natural. It took me a while to get back into the flow of the controls when I jumped back into the game years later. Makes replayability less likely when compared to games like Spider-Man and Assassin's Creed, which are generally easier to get back into after a long absence. 

Also, the open world is so empty and similar. Every area looks the same; rocky, hilly, desolate, and lifeless. Sure, it makes traversal using the magic fun, but there's so much more that could've been added. Also, the severe lack of side-quest activity is damning to the vast, underused open world. There's not much endgame content here. A few collection-based side-quests, and a bunch of unexplored towers and arenas/challenges. Personally, I spent a lot of time post-game trying to level up my magic, seeing as I beat the main story before utilizing even half of the vast magic system.

As I said before, the story is fine. Basic, but fine. The characters are also fine, if not forgettable. I've seen some people say she was too unlikable, but I never thought she was unlikable. I just think they're confusing unlikable personality with unlikable dialogue. The dialogue was so forced. Like an "edgy" teenager wrote the script. The cursing was excessive and the game isn't quite as funny as it thinks it is. But video game dialogue during cutscenes are often a little corny, it's not a dealbreaker.

Overall, this is a fun game. The biggest problem being a slow introduction, an underutilized world, and a bad scriptwriter. It felt a little undercooked, but definitely not bad by any stretch. Worth a try, especially seeing that the game is usually on sale every month.

user_reviews.author: Armand89
user_reviews.quote: A nice game with acceptable gameplay. The story of the game is interesting with surprises. A game with a too large open world but too much to explore without having missions in those areas but in the end it's an ok game to play

user_reviews.author: Chestex
user_reviews.quote:
Non capisco le recensioni da 0 o 1, davvero.. per compensare ne devo mettere una da 10 per forza. Il gioco ha un sistema di combattimento che è riuscito è molto divertente, tra i migliori se si tratta di magia, grafica buona ma non è mai la parte che conta, è un buon contorno, se c'è buono, altrimenti si va avanti. Il mondo è affascinante, il difetto forse è che è un po' vuoto, ma il parkour rapido aiuta per coloro che si annoiano. La storia nulla di epico, si fa seguire ma è il gameplay il fulcro secondo me, ed è davvero riuscito. Gli avrei dato 7,5/8 oggettivamente, ma ne metto dieci perché non merita tutti gli 0 e 1.

Ho trovato l’intro a New York davvero speciale, arriva come emozione la difficoltà di Frey, specie se il giocatore condivide con lei tali problemi, empatizza molto e arriva al cuore.
A me è arrivato.

user_reviews.author: PatoudeChatou
user_reviews.quote: Je ne suis pas d’accord avec toutes les critiques faites sur le jeu.Certes, il n’est pas parfait, mais cela reste un très bon jeu malgré tout. Le scénario est captivant, et le système de combat — bien qu’il demande un certain temps d’adaptation — devient très dynamique et intéressant une fois **** seul reproche que je pourrais lui faire, c’est son monde ouvert un peu trop vaste, qui n’apporte malheureusement pas grand-chose, si ce n’est du remplissage redondant et des collectibles disséminés un peu partout. Il manque de consistance et finit par devenir lassant sur la **** conclusion, j’ai passé un excellent moment sur ce jeu. J’ai pris beaucoup de plaisir à suivre Frey dans son aventure, et je suis sincèrement déçu qu’il ait reçu autant de critiques négatives — au point qu’il n’y aura sans doute jamais de suite.

user_reviews.quote: Nie rozumiem za bardzo silnego hejtu na tę grę, ale nie była zła, nie robiłem eksploracji, tylko szedłem z fabułą, która nawet mi się podobała. Minus za nieregularną grafikę, która raz była lepsza raz gorsza.

user_reviews.author: lumidemo

La historia me ha hecho reflexionar y el mundo esta bien. La gente se queja pero no he encontrado un bug. Lo acabe y se me paso el tiempo jugando pocos juegos hacen esto.

user_reviews.author: Kumokon
user_reviews.quote: The game has some issues, but they were definitely blown out of proportion. Hate bandwagoning is a real thing. Some dialog can be cringe, but not much more than a Kingdom Hearts or DMC game. Combat system is genuinely phenomenal, and performance/graphics for PS5 pro are good. Some color filtering choices are questionable, but the game looks pretty overall. Lore is very interesting, and character designs are stunning. Some songs are hauntingly beautiful, but the soundtrack has far too many generic, lietmotif-heavy, repetitive songs for me to ever listen to the soundtrack on my free time. Cutscenes are awkward and stilted unfortunately, but overall, this is a great game and has me glued to my seat. At 20 USD now, this game is definitely worth getting. It's really more of an 8, but I'm giving it a 10, since like FFXIII, this game suffers from hater syndrome.

user_reviews.author: Asusena
user_reviews.quote: Game is very good, don’t get the negative reviews. Gameplay consists of magic parkour and magic battles, very well done and entertaining even after 20+ hours. Graphical effects of spells are amazing to watch. Story is actually quite decent, feels fresh, and it’s not totally predictable. But what I liked the most was the feeling of progression and becoming more powerful after every improvement I got.  After playing this for a while you really feel like a magical being, a sorceress that can handle anything, it’s hard to describe but the battles feel epic, although it is challenging at times you can sense the power the character wields. user_reviews.author: LuciferCaeleste
user_reviews.quote: I enjoyed this game for the most part. Contrary to what most people have to say about this game, I like Frey. Most people have an issue with her because she isn't a cliché hero/heroine. She has personal baggage (due to various reasons/circumstances) that she works through throughout the story. I didn't see anything in her behavior resembling her acting entitled. She has a standoffish demeanor due to her childhood abandonment issues. These people complaining about her attitude wouldn't be nearly as pleasant as she is if they had a childhood like her. All the people who think this game is "woke" need to grow up and quit crying. If it isn't stereotypical macho misogynistic tropes objectifying women it's "woke." It's absurd, juvenile and stupid. I grew up on Arnold Schwarzenegger & Sylvester Stallone movies. I don't need or want every story being Commando Rambo. Frey is a breath of fresh air in a stagnant entertainment industry. If it isn't "woke" it's right wing macho crap. I'll take Frey over Kratos any day of the week. My biggest issues with this game are Cuff and the overall movement while exploring. MacCuffin s.u.c.k.s. I don't like anything about him, especially after finishing the main story. The movement is decent if you're using the parkour/speed option but it turns abysmal the moment you stop. I lost count of how many times Frey would get stuck on invisible objects in the terrain. This game isn't perfect but it was much better than I was expecting it to be considering how awful Squeenix is at everything.

user_reviews.author: Ladroconfuso

user_reviews.author: TheFUNisher423
user_reviews.quote:
The game is a lot of fun but has issues. I really enjoy the parkour & the combat system. The mechanic for switching between spells was really well done & makes you feel really powerful. No other game has made me really feel like I was in control of the magic I was using like this game. Switching between the types of magic & utilizing different spells in different situations was so well done & made me wish other games (thinking of Hogwarts Legacy, specifically) used a similar mechanic to make the flow of battle smoother.

I also enjoyed the story & the characters. The story gets a lot of hate online, along with the characters & voice acting, but I really do think that's just a bunch of incels/racists/misogynists who weren't happy to play as a black female. The story is a bit predictable, sure, it's the classic "chosen one" story, but so are like half the games out there & they don't get as much hate as this game for being predictable. The depth of the world building is great, & I really enjoyed a lot of the dialog, especially between the main character, Frey, & her "sidekick." They have an entertaining back-and-fourth throughout the game that is genuinely funny at times & engaging when they discuss deeper matters like Frey's past & the mysteries around the land of Athia.

On the negative side, the world is just too big. You can complete the whole storyline without even accessing half of the map. And after the story, there's no real push to explore the rest because there are no side quests. The "Detours" are shallow & there are only a handful of them. They give no real rewards & don't progress the story. A lot of the map is just empty space, & what is out there to explore is basically the same thing again & again. Every marker on the map is like, ""Defeat the enemy. Win a cloak,"" ""Defeat the enemy. Win a necklace,"" ""Defeat the enemy. Win some fingernail paint."" The combat is a lot of fun, but it's the ONLY thing to do in the game. There's one minor mechanic for sneaking up on "familiars," which are just cats with wings and/or horns, & each one takes like 10 seconds to do, & there are dozens of them. Everything else is just combat-based. ""Defeat these waves of enemies. Maybe defeat this boss at the end."" They should've broken it up with some racing missions utilizing the parkour or a couple of mini-games. And they should have had more towns or villages where people can be interacted with, because outside of the main city, there's just hostile lands with nothing but fighting & cat-taming.

The economy is a complete joke. For completing any of these missions, you get things like Old Coins. I ended the game with around 150 Old Coins. There are maybe 50 coins worth of items you can actually purchase & I already purchased all of them. Same for the "Mana" you gather to unlock spells. After you've unlocked them all, there's nothing to do with Mana at all. I ended the game with over 1000 Mana gathered & it **** that it's just there, doing nothing. This more than anything made the game & its side missions feel kind of pointless. There was no drive to complete most of the side quests because my reward is just more coins and Mana that I already can't spend.

The equipment is another issue. There are only 2 wearable items - cloak & necklace. And they can all be upgraded as high as you'd like using the same materials. But this means that once you've sunk a lot of those materials into one set, you don't want to have to start all over with a new set, even if you find something that you think looks cooler & you'd like to wear. Because each item you find starts out way lower than a set you've already invested in, so you'd have to spend all of your resources to get one set even up to par with what you're already using, when you could just continue to upgrade your existing set to higher levels. I only changed these items once early on in the game & after that, I couldn't justify starting over on new items at a much lower level than the set I was already wearing. I don't know what they were thinking when they decided to set the equipment up this way.

Overall, there is a lot of fun to be had here but it has major problems that keep it from being a "great" game. If more time & care was spent on the activities in the world & the rewards for completing them, this could've been an instant classic. Instead, it's just "pretty fun" with a lot of confusing choices made by the developers.

Forspoken suffers from really poor dialogue and unlikeable characters, repetitive gameplay and the overwhelming feeling is this is a project that should have really been cancelled early in development, but nobody ever pulled the trigger.

It's not a total write-off - visually it's OK, and there's some promise with the overall 'isekai/Alice in Wonderland' premise (unfortunately never realised here.) The sound design isn't terrible either. And the parkour type movement is, at least for a while, pretty decent.

But that's it. Everything else - gameplay, characters, dialogue, progression... everything - is pretty awful. But it's the writing that really kills it, because this thing is littered with cut scenes, all over the place, every few minutes, and every single one, without exception, is abysmal, with a script that feels it was written by a really bad AI. 

The lead character, Frey, is the worst character in the entire game. And it's not entirely the fault of the script either - she's badly acted, with weird delivery of the lines throughout that don't match the context of the situation.

So yeah, it's a poor game. It hasn't been unfairly blasted by a 'hate mob' - it's just a bad game.

I just finished this game and had mixed feelings.
Pros: 
1. The parkour system is unique and makes exploring a huge empty world more interesting.
2. The combat system is fun, with a wide variety of magic to try different combat styles. It feels under used after you get fire spells.
3. Story feels like a mix of Wizard of Oz with Alice in the Wonderland, which starts boring as heck, but the ending "twist" feels enjoyable.

2. Side quests (detours) are repetitive, boring and give no sense of reward. You do much of things that don't feel like you are helping anything get better.

I'm now in the post-end game hating even more the challenges required to get Platinum trophy. It feels so pointless that I might just give up and move on to a better game instead.

user_reviews.author: Chempion1
user_reviews.quote: Честно говоря, я не понял для кого вообще выпущена эта игра. У Square Enix уже есть своя Final Fantasy XVI, зачем ей понадобилась её плохая копия под названием Forspoken, не понятно? Итак. Мы имеем не очень красивый открытый мир, наполненный нечастыми существами, некоторых из которых иногда просто не видно в траве. Плюс к этому ужасную лицевую анимацию и скучнейший город-хаб. Всё остальное это не очень хорошая, как уже писал выше, копия Final Fantasy XVI. Ты бродишь по миру, убиваешь, собираешь, сражаешься с боссами, чьи силы ты потом и можешь частично использовать. Это силы: воды, огня, земли и мистификации. Знакомо, не правда ли? В игре есть уровни, но вот для чего они нужны вообще не понятно. За уровень выдают деньги (которые я так и не нашел где тратить) и очки прокачки. Но 70% этих очков ты всё равно тупо находишь в мире. Эта прокачка тоже достаточно странная, ты можешь выбрать ту или иную основную атаку, а вот доп. атаки (которые можно использовать раз, а потом дожидаться их восстановления) открываются в большом количестве, но настроить их порядок нельзя, какую ты не доиспользовал становится первой в следующем бою. Не очень удобно, часто просто забываешь, что включено заклинание которое в данный момент тебе и не нужно совсем. В игре есть паркур и он ужасен. Ты постоянно летишь туда, куда тебе не надо. Боссы достаточно незамысловатые, в отличие от тех же Айконов из Final Fantasy XVI, достаточно простые и не эпичные. Единственный который мне понравился это финальный босс, ну конечно только на фоне остальных. Управление тоже странное, на DualSense все боевые навыки повешены на два адаптивных тригера и вроде бы так и должно быть, но вы будете долбить по правому, особенно в начале игры, курку по несколько сотен раз за бой. Я понял, что ещё час и моторчики здохнут и отключил их, а через два я переназначил удары на "треугольник" и "квадрат" (хорошо хоть авторы догадались оставить такую возможность). Не очень удобно, но безопасно. Кстати очень много отзывов людей у которых DualSense всё-таки накрылся. Единственное, что мне правда понравилось в игре, так это закрученный сюжет, только за него 2 поставил, а не 0, но и здесь разработчики умудрились обосраться. Всю игру, ну %80 времени, вы будете изучать мир, вообще не понимая, кто вы и, что здесь происходит. И только после победы над третьим, ну может даже четвёртым, если дракона считать, боссом вам на голову вываливают весь этот сногсшибающий сюжет. Но подают его какими то флешбеками из прошедшей и неизвестной жизни нашей героини. Вы будете два часа бегать за яркой точкой, чтобы посмотреть на не анимированные 3D картинки, на которых иногда даже не понятно, что изображено. Вот тут вчитывайтесь в субтитры или вслушивайтесь в голоса. Интрига раскрывается. Ну вот нельзя было это обыграть как то поинтересней? Но всё, что я сказал ранее, это ерунда по сравнению с "толерантной атмосферой" самой игры. Знакомьтесь, нам предлагают: бездомную, грязную, наверно вонючую (воды то нет), вероятно судимую, 21 летнюю негpетянcкyю быдловатую девицу Фрею. И вот в её лице нас с самой первой минуты окунают в какой-то фем-БЛМоский ад. И если в "нашем" мире девки грабят банки, живут в халупе без воды! и рулят преступными бандами нью-йорка, да да в игровом нью-йорке этим занимаются именно девки. То фантастический мир Атии это реально матриархат. Всем правят женщины. Авторы просто взяли и поменяли роли полов в мире. Если девочки лазают по карманам и фехтуют на палках, то мальчики учатся справлять малую нужду сидя. В мире Атии 80% это женский пол. Да, яйценосны тоже есть, но это слюнтяи, подлецы, сумасшедшие и прочие отбросы общества. Вот ещё, все боссы, кроме финального, ну да бабы. Но так как женщины и негры априори злыми быть не могут, то в конце, открою тайну, все они окажутся на стороне добра. А наша независимая засранка станет, ну конечно владычицей всего мира, ни больше ни меньше. При том 80% нпс с которыми я общался это чернокожие. Да что там говорить, Гомер это кличка...кошки, не кота, ёлки палки, а кошки нашей героини! В Атии некоторые мужские персонажи говорят женскими голосами! Маразм! Как мне это лицемерие надоело уже! И вот я снова спрашиваю, а для кого выпущена эта игра? Для девочек? Ну судя по оценкам, девочек в неё играло невероятно мало. Для мальчиков? Зачем им играть в эту фем-блевотину, если есть Final Fantasy XVI? Вывод. Если хотите в ЭТО поиграть, дождитесь супер скидок, либо времени когда игра появится в подписке. Но самое главное! БЕРЕГИТЕ СВОЙ DUALSENSE!!!

user_reviews.author: Igl00Man
user_reviews.quote: Normally, PlayStation Open World games are very solid. Ghost Of Tsushima is the best game of this pairing, the Horizon series is also great, Spider-Man is a golden standard for the genre, and while not perfect, Final Fantasy 16 is also excellent. Forspoken's issues stem from the following. 1: The open world is devoid of meaningful side activities. 2: Enemies are too spongy, with unsatisfying combat. 3: The game is kind of drab to look at. 4: The story is very formulaic (if you've seen any Isekai anime, you know the story of Forspoken). And most importantly. 5: The protagonist isn't likeable, and doesn't have meaningful growth throughout the story. Paired with poor writing/voice over performances, the game was painful to go through at many points in time. The only positives is that the magic effects look nice, and the performance was smooth all throughout the experience. Even to the staunchest open world video game enjoyers, Forspoken needs to be skipped.

user_reviews.author: KrultySenpai
user_reviews.quote:
This game is a complete waste of time and money. I was really looking forward to this game and preordered the most expensive edition. I had a small hope that it would be better than my favorite game, Dragon's Dogma. Instead, I got a massive empty game that doesn't feel rewarding to play.

I give this game a half score for the movement which is smooth but feels automated and slow.  Ultimately, the movement doesn't give me enough freedom. I feel restricted.

I give the game two more score for the combat system (rounding the overall score from 2.5 to a two just because, as Freya like to say, f**k it). The magic is the best part about this game. It is a bit weird to get used to, but the effects are pretty cool which is all I have to say about it.

The map design paired with little variety of materials laying about makes this game feel more empty than it already is (absolutely atrocious to say the least).

The equipments are too simplistic. They should've focused on giving the equipments more stat and effects since this game has no weapon due to the focus on magic.

The dialogues, for the most part, feels like an opportunity for developing the characters are wasted. Even at the start, the dialogues is written in such a way as if the writer expected the players to have an in-depth knowledge about Frey.

Finally, the worst experience of the entire game is that the exploration is not rewarding. You went all that way to open a chest that gives you a material that is not worth while because crafting and upgrading ****! 

Overall, I just felt scammed to the point I had to make an account just to make my first non-Google Play store game review! Oh, and I was originally skeptical of the many negative reviews, but now I think they rated it too high. 

Also, this site is terrible for a submission from a mobile browser. It'd be a miracle for this review to posted...Forspoken t(-_-t) Edit: I ended up posting this months later due to the issue above.
